From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "cleared by both sides" and that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package". I'm not following it, and I recommend you don't either. Nothing in our file shows we cleared or accepted any of these positions. The [STANDARD] label comes from the Seller, and almost every item carrying it departs from our playbook. I've reviewed everything on its merits. In the cover reply, state expressly that no position is agreed, that everything remains subject to contract, and that the label has no effect. Otherwise silence could later be run as acquiescence.

## 1. Liability regime

| Item | Seller | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M | The Seller has landed exactly on our conditional fallback. We have no written authority from Amelia Frost for it, so we cannot accept it or signal flexibility. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. It would filter out most realistic claims. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x our figure, and the structure is wrong. A deductible basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k permanently. |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | This is our fallback, and it also needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which we don't have. Hold at 24. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Blanket | Limits apply only to General Warranty Claims | This is a hidden override. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into the general caps and time bars. Reverse the default so limits apply only where expressly stated. |

Do not offer or hint at 20% or 18 months in the mark-up. If the deal team wants to use either fallback, it needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft.

## 2. Fundamental/Title claims

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." Reject this. Title and capacity go to whether we are getting the asset at all. We need a separate regime with:
- a 100% cap (the price);
- at least six years;
- no de minimis, basket or knowledge bar.

## 3. Fraud, concealment and exclusivity (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

The limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. Our playbook requires a carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side can waive it. Also carve out specific indemnities and Fundamental claims from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.

## 4. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2:** The letter discloses the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records against everything. That is the deemed-disclosure approach we reject. It would hollow out the warranties, since almost any issue is "somewhere" in the data room. Require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
- **Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge):** This is a blanket exclusion covering anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or could have discovered from the data room or public records. It is effectively constructive knowledge plus prudent-search disclosure. Delete it. If the Seller needs any qualifier, it must be Seller knowledge, with named knowledge persons and a reasonable-enquiry standard. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Letter numbering:** Paragraph 1.3 is missing (1.2 jumps to 1.4). Ask what it was or whether text was removed.
- **Paragraph 1.4:** The "no admission" language is acceptable only if it doesn't undercut the warranty or indemnity position. Confirm it doesn't operate as a disclosure against anything.
- **Specific disclosures (paras 2–10):** These are useful, candid factual statements, and we should keep them on record. They should be tied to identified warranties, not left as general disclosure.

## 5. Specific deal issues

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6M, about 30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied "on delivery" of written consent. That fails on two points:
- Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Delivery isn't enough. DD-002 clause 11.3 attaches conditions to the consent.

Require an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent. The Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits neither exists yet.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2M).** The Seller proposes a release after Completion. The facility is unpaid with no discharge (Disclosure Letter para 3), and change-control clause 8.1 is engaged. Require:
- a current payout letter;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective security releases (including PPSR discharge) at Completion.

A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists. This is also a debt-free/cash-free point, so the payout must come out of the Seller's proceeds.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The Seller's note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" yet leaves them out of the funds flow. That is contradictory and risky. The bonuses are payable on Completion, so the Company, which we will own, is the likely payer. The Disclosure Letter also doesn't say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Require either a specific line item in the funds flow or an express Seller-funded mechanism that includes the triggered on-costs. Also reject the statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics." No such agreement exists.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010).** The Seller says an indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment is "adequate." Broaden it beyond the payment itself to cover IP ownership and infringement claims, and losses and costs arising from the Ironquay engagement. Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of every SOW3 fee triggers transfer of the Project Materials under clause 7.3, so require a confirmatory assignment on cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way (no bank evidence or receipt), so we should neither assert nor concede it.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and notification duty are unknown, so that characterisation is unsupported. We shouldn't assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure in either direction. Ask for:
- an obligation to preserve logs;
- investigation, with access and cooperation for us;
- regular updates up to Completion and afterwards;
- Seller conduct and notification decisions that don't prejudice us.

Also make sure Schedule 6 doesn't operate as a blanket disclosure against the privacy warranties.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls them ordinary-course costs, but the Disclosure Letter (para 8) says it doesn't state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Request the contracts and the terms for each. Assess before taking a position. Don't automatically treat them as Debt or seek a price deduction.

**Tax and IP.** The Seller says they are "settled under the general regime." Our position is that these terms remain open. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories and strike any wording that implies they are resolved or that the general regime overrides them. We shouldn't assume unlimited liability either.

**Title.** The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof, and the Disclosure Letter (para 10) concedes it identifies only the source relied on. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as:
- the share transfer history and issuance records;
- an ASIC extract;
- a PPSR search;
- confirmation of no options, pre-emption rights or third-party interests;
- board and shareholder authority for the sale.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The disclosure indicates neither needs consent merely because the shares are sold. This is low priority, but verify against the underlying documents before agreeing.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "efficiency note"** and reserve all positions in writing. Nothing is agreed.
2. **Hold the playbook numbers:** 25% / AUD 6M cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24 months. Do not offer 20% or 18 months without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Insert the fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. Reverse the "limits apply to all Claims" default.
5. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure,** and delete clause 8.3. Any knowledge qualifier must be Seller-side, with named persons and reasonable enquiry. Ask about missing para 1.3.
6. **Make Bluefen a condition precedent:** effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are met.
7. **Require Riverlark payout from Completion funds,** with effective security releases at Completion.
8. **Put the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs in the funds flow** or make them expressly Seller-funded.
9. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** and preserve the SOW3 cure with a confirmatory assignment.
10. **Handle DD-006 neutrally:** log preservation, investigation and updates, with no assumed breach and no numbers.
11. **Assess the Sandbar renewals** with no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
12. **Keep Tax and IP open and separate,** with no hidden general-regime override.
13. **Require independent title evidence,** not just the DD-012 register.
